title: Outdoor Cannabis: Season, Microclimate, Pollen and Weather Risk
summary: Outdoor cultivation replaces room-level environmental control with site selection and risk management across changing daylength, weather, water, pollen sources, wildlife and extreme events.

sections.title: Seasonal strategy starts with the site
sections.body: Latitude, frost dates, heat, rainfall, wind exposure, drainage and artificial night lighting shape the usable season. Cultivar development should be mapped onto these local risk windows rather than treated as a universal planting and harvest calendar.

sections.title: Pollen is a landscape-scale risk
sections.body: Windborne cannabis pollen deposition decreases strongly with distance but modeling shows a long-distance tail whose magnitude varies with meteorology and source conditions. Isolation is therefore risk reduction rather than a universally guaranteed zero-pollen distance.

sections.title: Extreme events affect both crops and people
sections.body: Wildfire survey research among cannabis producers documented smoke, ash, reduced light, operational disruption and worker-safety impacts. Outdoor contingency planning should prioritize emergency instructions and human safety before crop intervention.
